doc.title: Frank Capp interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: A busy weekend: Terry Gibbs, Supersax and Dixieland
summary: Capp describes his packed schedule of Terry Gibbs Dream Band, Supersax with L.A. Voices, bebop and Dixieland sets, and loving all kinds of playing.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: concert with Supersax. Now Med Flory has added a brass section to Supersax, and four voices. So it’s now the L.A. Voices he calls it. Sue Raney is the lead singer and the brass section, so it’s kind of, what do you call it, Supersax with voices? Or, I don’t know, it doesn’t matter what it’s called, it’s still big band and it’s fun to do. I like all kinds of playing. I enjoy doing what we’re doing here at this and I’m playing, I just finished, as I said, last night I went down and did a set with Terry Gibbs and Buddy DeFranco down at the other hotel. And that’s about as beboppish as you can get. And I just finished, I got off the stage downstairs doing an out-and-out Dixieland set you know. And I love it. I love it all.
You’ve got to change hats from one day to the next.

Right, sure. I mean a lot of, there was a day when a lot of hippy musicians thought that there was no validity in Dixieland or the traditional swing. But that’s not true. There’s great music everywhere.
Yeah. It’s really gratifying to be here and see, first of all, the old veterans. But then there’s some younger guys coming up too, who seem to have a pretty good handle on the classic swing.
